newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA DEALERS SEE STABLE LEV UNDER NEW GOVT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA DEALERS SEE STABLE LEV UNDER NEW GOVT.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev was expected to
trade stable between 1,500-1,600 to the dollar in the near term
if the new cabinet voted in office on Wednesday continued the
interim cabinet' financial stabilisation policy, dealers said.
The lev gained to 1,580-1,585 per dollar in light volume at
1230 GMT on the local interbank market on Wednesday from the
opening's 1,605-1,610 due to profit taking.
"If the new cabinet keeps its pledges to continue the
financial stabilisation policy of the interim cabinet, we may
see a relatively stable lev in the next couple of weeks," a
commercial bank dealer said.
The interim cabinet has signed a $657 million funding
agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF),
stabilised the lev to 1,500-1,600 per dollar from February's
record lows of 3,000-3,200 and brought inflation under control.
The parliament approved the leader of the Union of
Democratic Forces Ivan Kostov as prime minister and approved
his cabinet lineup and restructuring programme.
Introducing an IMF-prescribed currency board system,
carrying out economic reform, speeding privatisation and
encouraging foreign investments were among top priorities of
the new government outlined by Kostov in parliament.
The new Finance minister Muravei Radev said earlier on
Wednesday the currency board system, a form of fixed exchange
rate mechanism aimed at stabilising Bulgaria's shaky financial
sector and the fragile lev, would be introduced on July 1.
Expected lev stability between 1,500-1,600 per dollar
however would strongly depend on interest rate policies of the
Finance ministry and the central bank, another dealer said.
"Pressure could build up on the lev if yields on government
securities resume falling and it would be up to the central
bank to counter it," the dealer said.
The central bank had to intervene to support the lev on
Monday, when a cut in its main interest rate to 4.29 percent
monthly from 5.20 percent became effective and triggered a
dollar shortcovering.
The Bulgarian National Bank adjusts its main interest rate
weekly to the weighted average effective monthly yield of the
one- and four-week discount T-bills sold daily by the Finance
ministry.
-- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
